title: Cloud runs: a 3 s send window so Stop is free, then prompt-box batch of N as N parallel requests
description: Fabio, 2026-09-26. A cloud run bills the moment its POST leaves, and a mistake (wrong model, wrong settings) is usually caught in the first few seconds - by then the money is gone. Phase 1, the send window: every cloud run waits ~3 s before the POST, the card shows a visible 'Sending in 3...' countdown, and a Stop inside it cancels outright - card gone, nothing billed. One cancellable wait before the fetch in js/services/cloudExecutor.js, which already aborts free before the POST (MPI-928), so the agent's cloud runs get it too. Local runs untouched. Phase 2, prompt-box batch for cloud: a batch of N on a model with no native batch fans out to N parallel requests after ONE shared window, all N cards drawn up front (the agent's MPI-870/876 fan-out is the prior art). Cue price reads xN (N bills, unlike a native batch's one). Stop in the window kills all N free; after it, each card keeps what it paid for (MPI-928/929). Most proprietary video platforms batch four; power users roll four Seedance takes and keep the best. Today the box's batch shows only where the provider batches natively (FLUX Schnell, Veo) - which is why MPI-899's Nano Banana never offered one.
